pageCache.pageTitle: The Ilsleys Primary School | The Ilsleys Primary  |  Berkshire, UK
pageCache.text:
We believe in providing the best opportunities for our children of all ages and abilities. We strongly feel that we “achieve more together” and can really make a difference in our children’s lives by building a partnership with our families. Our children demonstrate outstanding behaviour and really are a joy to teach. Our staff are fully involved in the daily life of the school to ensure that our children get the most out of their learning, enjoy their school and make a positive contribution to our community.
Please come and visit our school to find out more.
The Ilsleys Primary School and Hampstead Norreys Church of England Primary School are now federated. We had a successful collaboration for nearly four years and naturally progressed onto federation. The school shares a Headteacher, Miss K.House as well as having an established leadership team that work together for both schools. They meet fortnightly and plan and work on various aspects of school improvement. The links between the two schools are very strong as a result of this, staff training takes place every week where both schools come together. Both schools plan and organise ‘challenge’ days where the children from both schools go across to each others school for a different learning experience. Both schools have a fun, family orientated feel to them where children love learning in an environment that is nurturing and caring. The staff are dedicated to ensuring all our children get the best education they can as well as feeling cared for and valued as people. We do an excellent job in preparing our children for the future which makes these two schools wonderful places to learn.
Please contact the School Office on 01635 281225 to arrange a visit. We will be delighted to see you.
Executive Headteacher

At Hampstead Norreys and The Ilsleys Federation, we believe that all pupils have the ability to love Maths. We work hard to develop a growth mindset in children and a ‘can do’ attitude to Mathematics. We believe that, through quality first teaching, regular practise, collaborative learning and immediate intervention that all children have the potential to ‘go deeper’ and broaden their understanding of mathematical concepts.
We understand the importance of Mathematics in the wider world and encourage pupils to be reflective about how key concepts can be used in real life. We encourage them to make connections in their learning between different concepts and believe that all pupils should have the opportunity to develop, fluency, reasoning and problem-solving skills. We believe that, after developing true fluency, children need the opportunity to show that they can apply their knowledge and then move on even further to prove they have mastered the concept through detailed explanations.
Pupils in our school are reflective learners. Meta-cognition, especially working systematically and showing good reasoning skills, are at the heart of our Maths learning. The pupils in KS2 are keen to record their learning and the strategies they have used in their learning diaries. These provide a good foundation for when key concepts are re-visited across the year.
In terms of assessment, we have developed our curriculum to allow teachers and learners to achieve a secure and deep understanding of each mathematical concept. Key objectives are re-visited each term and built on throughout the year. This is evidenced in our assessment rubric. It is designed to give us the opportunity to address key points individually, ensure that children have a secure and deep understanding of those points, before offering the opportunity to ‘go deeper’ within them. Our aim is for all pupils to master the full Mathematics curriculum for their age range.

pageCache.text:
Government Statement
The government is providing additional funding of £150 million per annum to improve provision of physical education (PE) and sport in primary schools. This funding – provided jointly by the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, Media and Sport – will be allocated to primary school head teachers.
This funding is ring-fenced and therefore can only be spent on provision of PE and sport in schools. Funding for schools will be calculated by reference to the number of primary-aged pupils (between the ages of 5 and 11), as recorded in the annual schools census in January.
Schools must spend the additional funding on improving their provision of PE and sport, but they will have the freedom to choose how they do this.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum Information | The Ilsleys Primary School
pageCache.text:
At Hampstead Norreys and The Ilsleys Primary School, our aim is for all children to be able to develop a vision of their future and an awareness of the opportunities to help them realise this. We aim for every pupil to leave with a sense of pride that they have developed the confidence, skills and general knowledge needed to achieve success. Our curriculum provides opportunities for children to develop as independent, confident and successful learners, with high aspirations, who know how to make a positive contribution to their community and the wider society.
Our intention is that our curriculum opens children’s eyes to the world within and beyond their immediate environment and its possibilities and helps them to make connections with their own lives. Our themes connect learning across subjects throughout each year, helping children to make links to possible jobs, travel, hobbies and community work they may aspire to in the future. Enrichment activities, such as trips and visitors enhance and build on our pupils’ ‘cultural capital’, offering experiences that many of our pupils wouldn’t otherwise have access to. We aim to widen pupils’ opportunities and inspire all of our children to gain the knowledge and skills they will need to achieve the future they aspire to.
Welcome to Hampstead Norreys and The Ilsleys Primary Schools. To find information about the curriculum and the subjects we offer, please look at the subject links.

The staff at both schools believe that art enables children to communicate what they say, think and feel.
